content:
Maya: Heads up — p99 queue depth on eu-west GPU pool jumped after yesterday's traffic spike, looks token-related not GPU throttling. anyone seen this?
Raj: Can you paste the token accounting snapshot? p50/p95/p99 tokens/sec per-GPU?
Maya: Copied from dashboard:
```
pool: eu-west-gpu-32
per_gpu_tpm_capacity=32000
observed_tokens_s=12500
p99_queue_ms=420
kv_cache_hit=0.68
``` 
So per-gpu appears under-provisioned for this request mix (long ctx, low cache hits).
Sophie: Hmm. sounds like our current per-customer hard TPMs are double-counting when regional-fallback routes hit multiple pools. We should smear reserved fallback capacity and subtract it from available tokens before computing soft admission.
Liam: +1. Also we should treat fallback-reserved as a separate credit pool. If we don't, admission thinks it has X tokens and routes, then fallback storms drain both origin+fallback -> saturation.
Maya: proposal: compute effective_pool_tokens = raw_pool_capacity - fallback_reserve_tokens; then admission uses leaky bucket with EWMA refill where refill = effective_pool_tokens * (1 - backlog_penalty).
Raj: backlog_penalty formula idea: penalty = min(0.5, alpha * normalized_queue_depth) — keeps small spikes from killing refill rate. alpha ~ 0.02
Sophie: I'd rather run a 10k-sim with the new formula. Also add per-request token-weight for KV-miss (weight 1.8) vs KV-hit (weight 1.0). That aligns accounting with observed cost.
capacity-bot: recompute done — recommended soft_tpm_limit per-gpu=26000 (was 30000), fallback_reserve=2400 tokens/gpu, kv_miss_multiplier=1.8
ops-bot: deploy alert: adm-controller v2.3.1 deployed to eu-west at 2026-03-18T09:15Z
Liam: can we throttle new sessions with token-based admission (soft) and only flip to hard deny above 3x queue target? avoid abrupt failures.
Maya: plan: run sim (Sophie), push config to staging (Raj), monitor p95 latency and queue. sync in 30m in #eng-infra. @Sophie @Raj
Sophie: on it :mag:
Raj: will push a canary with 10% traffic to eu-west-staging
Maya: :thumbsup: Thanks all — should prevent cascading fallback storms.
